newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks slightly higher in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks slightly higher in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks put on modest gains at the open on Monday morning, with most traders and investors waiting for a clearer market direction, brokers said.
"I think the market on the net trading side should be quite steady, but traders and investors are both unwilling to do too much," said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
The Hang Seng Index put on 20 points to trade at 12,551 in early morning trade. Turnover was a respectable HK$859 million.
"We saw some weakness on Wall Street last Friday and the (Hong Kong) futures are trading at a slight discount," Li said.
Hang Seng Index futures' November contract declined 18 points to trade at 12,551, trading at a slight discount to the cash market in the first half hour of trading.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost seven to 6,022 on Friday.
"Hong Kong outperformed other Asia regional markets last week and should take a breather in advance of the U.S. election," said Conal Sanjana, institutional sales manager at Kerry Securities.
The United States goes to the polls on Tuesday.
Properties led the gainers. Conversely, only the utility sector declined.
New World Development leaped HK$1.40 to HK$47.40, mainly due to the successful issue of convertible bonds worth US$350 million, brokers said.
The company will release its result for the year ended June 30 on Thursday.
"There is little excitement in the utility sector," said Amsteel's Li

China Light eased HK$0.20 to HK$36.00. The company will report its earnings results for the year ended September 30, 1996. Most analysts are expecting a 13 percent dip in earnings in FY96, brokers said.
The company announced that it had signed a preliminary agreement to build a gas-fired power plant in Shenzhen.
"This news has been out, but it is good to see confirmation of it," said Sanjana.
Hong Kong Telecom was unchanged in early trading at HK$13.55. The company will report earnings on Tuesday. Analysts are forecasting growth of about 15 percent for the six months to September 1996.
